name: apilevel
doc: String constant stating the supported DB-API level. Required by the DB-API. Hard-coded to "2.0".

name: Blob
doc: A Blob instance is a file-like object that can read and write data in an SQLite BLOB. Call len(blob) to get the size (number of bytes) of the blob. Use indices and slices for direct access to the blob data.

name: close
doc: Close the blob.

name: read
doc:
Read data at the current offset position.

  length
    Read length in bytes.

If the end of the blob is reached, the data up to end of file will
be returned.  When length is not specified, or is negative,
Blob.read() will read until the end of the blob.

name: seek
doc:
Set the current access position to offset.

The origin argument defaults to os.SEEK_SET (absolute blob
positioning).  Other values for origin are os.SEEK_CUR (seek
relative to the current position) and os.SEEK_END (seek relative to
the blob's end).

name: tell
doc: Return the current access position for the blob.

name: write
doc:
Write data at the current offset.

This function cannot change the blob length.  Writing beyond the end
of the blob will result in an exception being raised.

name: complete_statement
doc: Checks if a string contains a complete SQL statement.

name: connect
signatures: connect(database, *, timeout=5.0, detect_types=0, isolation_level='DEFERRED', check_same_thread=True, factory=sqlite3.Connection, cached_statements=128, uri=False, autocommit=sqlite3.LEGACY_TRANSACTION_CONTROL)
doc:
Open a connection to the SQLite database file 'database'.

You can use ":memory:" to open a database connection to a database that
resides in RAM instead of on disk.

changed.text: Added the uri parameter.
database can now also be a path-like object, not only a string.
Added the sqlite3.connect/handle auditing event.
Added the autocommit parameter.
All parameters except database are now keyword-only.

name: Connection
doc: SQLite database connection object.

changed.text: A ResourceWarning is emitted if close() is not called before a Connection object is deleted.

name: autocommit
doc: This attribute controls PEP 249-compliant transaction behaviour. autocommit has three allowed values:

name: backup
doc: Makes a backup of the database.

name: blobopen
doc:
Open and return a BLOB object.

table
  Table name.
column
  Column name.
rowid
  Row id.
readonly
  Open the BLOB without write permissions.
name
  Database name.

name: close
doc:
Close the database connection.

Any pending transaction is not committed implicitly.

name: commit
doc:
Commit any pending transaction to the database.

If there is no open transaction, this method is a no-op.

name: create_aggregate
doc: Creates a new aggregate.

changed.text: All three parameters are now positional-only.

name: create_collation
doc: Creates a collation function.

changed.text: The collation name can contain any Unicode character. Earlier, only ASCII characters were allowed.

name: create_function
doc: Creates a new function.

changed.text: Added the deterministic parameter.
The first three parameters are now positional-only.

name: create_window_function
doc:
Creates or redefines an aggregate window function. Non-standard.

name
  The name of the SQL aggregate window function to be created or
  redefined.
num_params
  The number of arguments the step and inverse methods takes.
aggregate_class
  A class with step(), finalize(), value(), and inverse() methods.
  Set to None to clear the window function.

name: cursor
doc: Return a cursor for the connection.

name: deserialize
doc:
Load a serialized database.

  data
    The serialized database content.
  name
    Which database to reopen with the deserialization.

The deserialize interface causes the database connection to
disconnect from the target database, and then reopen it as
an in-memory database based on the given serialized data.

The deserialize interface will fail with SQLITE_BUSY if the database
is currently in a read transaction or is involved in a backup
operation.

name: enable_load_extension
doc: Enable dynamic loading of SQLite extension modules.

changed.text: Added the sqlite3.enable_load_extension auditing event.

name: execute
doc: Executes an SQL statement.

name: executemany
doc: Repeatedly executes an SQL statement.

name: executescript
doc: Executes multiple SQL statements at once.

name: getconfig
doc:
Query a boolean connection configuration option.

op
  The configuration verb; one of the sqlite3.SQLITE_DBCONFIG codes.

name: getlimit
doc:
Get connection run-time limits.

category
  The limit category to be queried.

name: in_transaction
doc: This read-only attribute corresponds to the low-level SQLite autocommit mode.

name: interrupt
doc: Abort any pending database operation.

name: isolation_level
doc: Controls the legacy transaction handling mode of sqlite3. If set to None, transactions are never implicitly opened. If set to one of "DEFERRED", "IMMEDIATE", or "EXCLUSIVE", corresponding to the underlying SQLite transaction behaviour, implicit transaction management is performed.

name: iterdump
doc:
Returns iterator to the dump of the database in an SQL text format.

filter
  An optional LIKE pattern for database objects to dump

changed.text: Added the filter parameter.

name: load_extension
doc: Load SQLite extension module.

changed.text: Added the sqlite3.load_extension auditing event.
Added the entrypoint parameter.

name: rollback
doc:
Roll back to the start of any pending transaction.

If there is no open transaction, this method is a no-op.

name: row_factory
doc: The initial row_factory for Cursor objects created from this connection. Assigning to this attribute does not affect the row_factory of existing cursors belonging to this connection, only new ones. Is None by default, meaning each row is returned as a tuple.

changed.text: Deleting the row_factory attribute is no longer allowed.

name: serialize
doc:
Serialize a database into a byte string.

  name
    Which database to serialize.

For an ordinary on-disk database file, the serialization is just
a copy of the disk file.  For an in-memory database or a "temp"
database, the serialization is the same sequence of bytes which
would be written to disk if that database were backed up to disk.

name: set_authorizer
doc: Set authorizer callback.

changed.text: Added support for disabling the authorizer using None.
The only parameter is now positional-only.

name: set_progress_handler
doc:
Set progress handler callback.

  progress_handler
    A callable that takes no arguments.
    If the callable returns non-zero, the current query is
    terminated, and an exception is raised.
  n
    The number of SQLite virtual machine instructions that are
    executed between invocations of 'progress_handler'.

If 'progress_handler' is None or 'n' is 0, the progress handler is
disabled.

changed.text: The first parameter is now positional-only.

name: set_trace_callback
doc: Set a trace callback called for each SQL statement (passed as unicode).

changed.text: The first parameter is now positional-only.

name: setconfig
doc:
Set a boolean connection configuration option.

op
  The configuration verb; one of the sqlite3.SQLITE_DBCONFIG codes.

name: setlimit
doc:
Set connection run-time limits.

  category
    The limit category to be set.
  limit
    The new limit. If the new limit is a negative number, the limit
    is unchanged.

Attempts to increase a limit above its hard upper bound are silently
truncated to the hard upper bound. Regardless of whether or not the
limit was changed, the prior value of the limit is returned.

name: text_factory
doc: A callable that accepts a bytes parameter and returns a text representation of it. The callable is invoked for SQLite values with the TEXT data type. By default, this attribute is set to str.

changed.text: Deleting the text_factory attribute is no longer allowed.

name: total_changes
doc: Return the total number of database rows that have been modified, inserted, or deleted since the database connection was opened.

name: Cursor
doc: SQLite database cursor class.

name: arraysize
doc: Read/write attribute that controls the number of rows returned by fetchmany(). The default value is 1 which means a single row would be fetched per call.

changed.text: Negative values are rejected by raising ValueError.

name: close
doc: Closes the cursor.

name: connection
doc: Read-only attribute that provides the SQLite database Connection belonging to the cursor. A Cursor object created by calling con.cursor() will have a connection attribute that refers to con:

name: description
doc: Read-only attribute that provides the column names of the last query. To remain compatible with the Python DB API, it returns a 7-tuple for each column where the last six items of each tuple are None.

name: execute
doc: Executes an SQL statement.

changed.text: ProgrammingError is emitted if named placeholders are used and parameters is a sequence instead of a dict.

name: executemany
doc: Repeatedly executes an SQL statement.

changed.text: ProgrammingError is emitted if named placeholders are used and the items in parameters are sequences instead of dicts.

name: executescript
doc: Executes multiple SQL statements at once.

name: fetchall
doc: Fetches all rows from the resultset.

name: fetchmany
doc:
Fetches several rows from the resultset.

size
  The default value is set by the Cursor.arraysize attribute.

changed.text: Negative size values are rejected by raising ValueError.

name: fetchone
doc: Fetches one row from the resultset.

name: lastrowid
doc: Read-only attribute that provides the row id of the last inserted row. It is only updated after successful INSERT or REPLACE statements using the execute() method. For other statements, after executemany() or executescript(), or if the insertion failed, the value of lastrowid is left unchanged. The initial value of lastrowid is None.

changed.text: Added support for the REPLACE statement.

name: row_factory
doc: Control how a row fetched from this Cursor is represented. If None, a row is represented as a tuple. Can be set to the included sqlite3.Row; or a callable that accepts two arguments, a Cursor object and the tuple of row values, and returns a custom object representing an SQLite row.

changed.text: Deleting the row_factory attribute is no longer allowed.

name: rowcount
doc: Read-only attribute that provides the number of modified rows for INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, and REPLACE statements; is -1 for other statements, including CTE queries. It is only updated by the execute() and executemany() methods, after the statement has run to completion. This means that any resulting rows must be fetched in order for rowcount to be updated.

name: setinputsizes
doc: Required by DB-API. Does nothing in sqlite3.

name: setoutputsize
doc: Required by DB-API. Does nothing in sqlite3.

name: DatabaseError
doc: Exception raised for errors that are related to the database. This serves as the base exception for several types of database errors. It is only raised implicitly through the specialised subclasses. DatabaseError is a subclass of Error.

name: DataError
doc: Exception raised for errors caused by problems with the processed data, like numeric values out of range, and strings which are too long. DataError is a subclass of DatabaseError.

name: enable_callback_tracebacks
doc: Enable or disable callback functions throwing errors to stderr.

name: Error
doc: The base class of the other exceptions in this module. Use this to catch all errors with one single except statement. Error is a subclass of Exception.

name: sqlite_errorcode
doc: The numeric error code from the SQLite API

name: sqlite_errorname
doc: The symbolic name of the numeric error code from the SQLite API

name: IntegrityError
doc: Exception raised when the relational integrity of the database is affected, e.g. a foreign key check fails. It is a subclass of DatabaseError.

name: InterfaceError
doc: Exception raised for misuse of the low-level SQLite C API. In other words, if this exception is raised, it probably indicates a bug in the sqlite3 module. InterfaceError is a subclass of Error.

name: InternalError
doc: Exception raised when SQLite encounters an internal error. If this is raised, it may indicate that there is a problem with the runtime SQLite library. InternalError is a subclass of DatabaseError.

name: LEGACY_TRANSACTION_CONTROL
doc: Set autocommit to this constant to select old style (pre-Python 3.12) transaction control behaviour. See Transaction control via the isolation_level attribute for more information.

name: NotSupportedError
doc: Exception raised in case a method or database API is not supported by the underlying SQLite library. For example, setting deterministic to True in create_function(), if the underlying SQLite library does not support deterministic functions. NotSupportedError is a subclass of DatabaseError.

name: OperationalError
doc: Exception raised for errors that are related to the database’s operation, and not necessarily under the control of the programmer. For example, the database path is not found, or a transaction could not be processed. OperationalError is a subclass of DatabaseError.

name: paramstyle
doc: String constant stating the type of parameter marker formatting expected by the sqlite3 module. Required by the DB-API. Hard-coded to "qmark".

name: PARSE_COLNAMES
doc: Pass this flag value to the detect_types parameter of connect() to look up a converter function by using the type name, parsed from the query column name, as the converter dictionary key. The query column name must be wrapped in double quotes (") and the type name must be wrapped in square brackets ([]).

name: PARSE_DECLTYPES
doc: Pass this flag value to the detect_types parameter of connect() to look up a converter function using the declared types for each column. The types are declared when the database table is created. sqlite3 will look up a converter function using the first word of the declared type as the converter dictionary key. For example:

name: PrepareProtocol
doc: PEP 246 style object adaption protocol type.

name: ProgrammingError
doc: Exception raised for sqlite3 API programming errors, for example supplying the wrong number of bindings to a query, or trying to operate on a closed Connection. ProgrammingError is a subclass of DatabaseError.

name: register_adapter
doc: Register a function to adapt Python objects to SQLite values.

name: register_converter
doc: Register a function to convert SQLite values to Python objects.

name: Row
doc: A Row instance serves as a highly optimized row_factory for Connection objects. It supports iteration, equality testing, len(), and mapping access by column name and index.

changed.text: Added support of slicing.

name: keys
doc: Returns the keys of the row.

doc: Flags that should be returned by the authorizer_callback callable passed to Connection.set_authorizer(), to indicate whether:

name: sqlite_version
doc: Version number of the runtime SQLite library as a string.

name: sqlite_version_info
doc: Version number of the runtime SQLite library as a tuple of integers.

name: threadsafety
doc: Integer constant required by the DB-API 2.0, stating the level of thread safety the sqlite3 module supports. This attribute is set based on the default threading mode the underlying SQLite library is compiled with. The SQLite threading modes are:

changed.text: Set threadsafety dynamically instead of hard-coding it to 1.

name: Warning
doc: This exception is not currently raised by the sqlite3 module, but may be raised by applications using sqlite3, for example if a user-defined function truncates data while inserting. Warning is a subclass of Exception.
